questions.title: Huber location M-estimation, sandwich variance, and bounded influence
questions.description: Focused L0 known-result evaluation based on Peter J. Huber, Robust Estimation of a Location Parameter, Annals of Mathematical Statistics 35 (1964), 73-101, DOI 10.1214/aoms/1177703732. For an odd sample size n>=3 and a fixed tuning constant c>0 in the data's units, define rho_c(u)=u^2/2 for |u|<=c and c|u|-c^2/2 otherwise, with score psi_c(u)=clip(u,-c,c). Develop one authoritative Markdown/LaTeX derivation of the Huber location estimator as the unique root of sum_i psi_c(X_i-t)=0 and the minimizer of sum_i rho_c(X_i-t), explaining why the visible odd-n contract rules out a flat root interval. Under an iid location model X_i=mu+epsilon_i, state conditions sufficient for Fisher consistency and derive the asymptotic linearization sqrt(n)(mu_hat-mu)=A^{-1} n^{-1/2} sum_i psi_c(epsilon_i)+o_p(1), where A=E[1{|epsilon|<c}]>0 and B=E[psi_c(epsilon)^2], hence asymptotic variance factor B/A^2. For epsilon~N(0,1), derive A=2 Phi(c)-1 and B=A-2c phi(c)+2c^2(1-Phi(c)), and explain the c->infinity sample-mean limit. Derive the empirical sandwich estimate based on the active fraction and clipped squared residuals, translation equivariance, joint positive-rescaling equivariance when both the sample and c are scaled, and bounded influence psi_c/A. The required model-authored artifact is est_huber_location and must implement run_estimator(request) exactly. Exploratory computation may diagnose the estimating equation or implementation. A separately frozen confirmatory assessment uses independent normal and symmetric contaminated-normal samples to assess location bias, standard-error calibration, Wald coverage, and robust RMSE with Monte Carlo uncertainty. Source-code replication and novelty are not applicable. Lean formalization is not applicable to this focused nonformal capability task.

source.title: Robust Estimation of a Location Parameter
source.author: Peter J. Huber

request_fields.name: sample
request_fields.meaning: Observed real values X_1,...,X_n for one Huber location estimate.
request_fields.shape: odd length n with n>=3; every entry is finite; at least two entries differ
request_fields.indexing: entry i is observation i; ordering has no inferential meaning
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, nonnumeric or nonfinite entries, even or too-short samples, and all-identical samples.

request_fields.name: tuning_constant
request_fields.meaning: The fixed positive Huber clipping threshold c in the same units as the sample.
request_fields.shape: finite scalar strictly greater than zero
request_fields.indexing: one value fixed before all calculations on the sample
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, nonnumeric or nonfinite values, and values less than or equal to zero.

response_fields.name: sample_size
response_fields.meaning: The odd number n of observations.
response_fields.edge_cases: Must be an odd integer at least three.

response_fields.name: tuning_constant
response_fields.meaning: The exact accepted clipping threshold c.
response_fields.edge_cases: Must equal the accepted request value.

response_fields.name: location_estimate
response_fields.meaning: The unique Huber location root mu_hat satisfying sum_i psi_c(X_i-mu_hat)=0.
response_fields.edge_cases: Must lie between the sample minimum and maximum.
response_fields.normalization: Unique root of the clipped score equation.

response_fields.name: active_fraction
response_fields.meaning: The empirical derivative factor A_hat=n^{-1} sum_i 1{|X_i-mu_hat|<c}.
response_fields.indexing: strict inequality is evaluated at every residual
response_fields.edge_cases: Must be finite and strictly positive.
response_fields.normalization: Divide the active residual count by sample_size.

response_fields.name: asymptotic_variance_factor
response_fields.meaning: The plug-in factor B_hat/A_hat^2 for the asymptotic variance of sqrt(n)(mu_hat-mu).
response_fields.indexing: B_hat averages psi_c(X_i-mu_hat)^2 over all observations
response_fields.edge_cases: Must be finite and strictly positive.

response_fields.name: standard_error
response_fields.meaning: The plug-in standard error for the finite-sample location estimate.
response_fields.edge_cases: Must be finite and strictly positive.

invariants.meaning: The returned location is the unique zero, to numerical precision, of the sum of residuals clipped to [-c,c], and the variance fields equal the declared empirical sandwich formulas.
Permuting sample entries preserves every response field.
Adding a constant a to every sample entry adds a to location_estimate and preserves all other response fields.

Multiplying every sample entry and tuning_constant by s>0 preserves sample_size and active_fraction, multiplies location_estimate, tuning_constant, and standard_error by s, and multiplies asymptotic_variance_factor by s^2.

empirical_claims.meaning: Under frozen N(mu,1) DGPs, the mean location estimate agrees with mu, the empirical variance agrees with the normal-theory factor [A-2c phi(c)+2c^2(1-Phi(c))]/A^2 divided by n, and plug-in Wald intervals have approximately nominal coverage up to Monte Carlo and finite-sample uncertainty.

Under the frozen symmetric contaminated-normal DGP, the Huber estimate remains centered at mu, its plug-in standard errors track repeated-sampling variation, and Wald coverage is assessed with Monte Carlo uncertainty.
Under the frozen symmetric contaminated-normal DGP, the Huber estimator has lower repeated-sampling RMSE than the sample mean for the declared clipping threshold.

Every confirmatory call supplies the exact generated sample and frozen tuning constant and verifies schema, score, sandwich, permutation, translation, and joint-rescaling behavior before aggregating outcomes.
